Definition: to be (causatively, make) right (in a moral or forensic sense)
BiblicalUsage: Tsadaq is the word for being right, and for being declared right. Judah confessed that Tamar was more righteous than he; the judges were told to justify the righteous and condemn the wicked; and Isaiah says the righteous servant will justify many. It covers both the life that is right before God and the verdict that declares it so.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe righteousness is not something we achieve and offer to God — it is His verdict, and His gift. My position is that the only righteousness that stands is the one God declares, and in Christ He declares it over sinners who trust Him. That is why Daniel says those who turn many to righteousness will shine like the stars.
